newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin says no plan to use budget reserve.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin says no plan to use budget reserve.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Wednesday he would not use the C$2.5 billion ($1.8 billion) contingency reserve budgeted for the 1996/97 financial year unless he had to cover unexpected needs.
Martin indicated he has not had to use it so far this year.
"No, it's there to cover the unexpected," Martin told Reuters in an inverview after the release of his autumn budget update.

In the update, Martin pegged the final 1995/96 deficit at C$28.6 billion ($20.9 billion), C$4.1 billion ($3 billion) below what he had originally projected, with C$2.5 billon (S$1.8 billion) of that coming from the unused contingency reserve.

"Now, you never know what the unexpected is going to be, ... the definition of the unexpected is that I can't tell you what it's going to be. But we will do the same thing, if we don't need (the reserve), we won't use it," Martin said, adding that his deficit target for 1996/97 remained at C$24.3 billion ($17.7 billion), the same as his projection in the budget released in March.
"As far as I am concerned, the target is C$24.3 (billion), that's what I said, if we do better -- fine," Martin said.
